analysis.title: Micron Earnings Preview: Another Beat And Guide Above Street... But SCAs May Cap Upside Surprise
key_insights: Goldman expects Micron to beat on the August-quarter print and guide the November quarter above consensus ($57.7BN vs $56.7BN). The Q4 print is 'largely well understood', so the market is focused on the November guide.

GS semis analyst Jim Schneider is above the Street across the board for the November quarter. Median sellside estimates are revenue $51.49B, gross margin 86.2% and EPS $31.83. If Goldman is right, quarterly revenue goes from $41.5B in May to nearly $58B by November, a 40% jump in two quarters.
Positioning into the print 'feels relatively balanced' per GS TMT specialist Peter Callahan. Micron is about 10% below its all-time high, while Samsung and Hynix are still 20-40% below theirs.

Strategic Customer Agreements (long-term contracts with floor pricing) are expected to limit the size of the beat. More output locked into SCAs means less spot-price upside, which helps earnings durability but cuts the size of the beats seen over the last ~6 quarters (EPS beats of 10-30%).

Callahan's five talking points: the November revenue guide vs the Street (up ~10% q/q) and the pace of y/y and q/q deceleration, SCA updates, capex vs capital returns in FY27, HBM share (investors want Micron to hold or grow ~20%), and industry supply/demand especially China.
Capital returns could steal the show. Micron has net cash of ~$24.4B and $18.3B adjusted FCF last quarter. GS's Narain flags commentary on buybacks 'post CHIPS restrictions' as top of mind.

JPMorgan's Harlan Sur calls the December 9 CHIPS Act anniversary 'a capital return inflection point', after which Micron has committed to returning 100% of excess cash (buybacks primary). He sees cumulative FCF approaching $200B through year-end 2027.

Sur's base case for the 10-K SCA disclosure is bit production coverage of 35%+ (from ~20% DRAM and ~33% NAND last quarter), possibly already 50%+. Floor pricing would lock in gross margins 'well above' the prior ~62% peak.
Goldman's desk flags progress on the 16+ long-term SCAs, including deposits and visibility on the previously referenced $100bn+ of minimum commitments, as a key watchpoint.

GS Asia view (Narain): memory stocks in the region remain 'fundamentally compelling but have suffered from relative OW positioning in a period of intense de-grossing'. Debates are short-term data center construction, medium-term 2028 earnings, long-term whether LTAs changed the memory cycle, and AI funding sustainability plus China's CXMT supply.
Per GS, 60% of US data centers planned for completion in 2027 have not started construction, mostly due to power constraints.

Korea flow angle (GS Seoul, Heather Oh): Samsung's W15TN buyback is 87% complete and SK Hynix's W40TN program is ~75% done, both finishing early October. Foreigners and retail were joint net sellers of both in September, raising concern about a liquidity void once buybacks end.
GS's Graham Ambrose notes Hynix (local) and Kioxia have underperformed the Hynix ADR and Micron since July. Kioxia trades at 3.3x March-2028 P/E with 101% ROE and 116% upside to GS's ¥38,667 target.

Prior quarter (reported June 24): revenue $41.5B vs $35.7B expected, gross margin 84.9% vs 81.9%, August-quarter guide of $49-51B, about $7B above the Street. SK Hynix rose 11% and Kioxia up to 15% the next morning.

market_movers.rationale: Goldman expects a beat with about 3% revenue upside to the Street and a November guide of $57.7B vs $56.7B consensus. SCAs may limit the size of the EPS surprise.
Kioxia has 116% upside to the GS target of ¥38,667, trading at 3.3x March-2028 P/E with a 101% ROE.

sector_views.rationale: GS expects persistent DRAM/NAND tightness to support pricing, with EPS mid-single-digit percentages above consensus for Q3-Q4 2027 on better mix and pricing.

earnings_insights: Micron August-quarter (fiscal Q4) print due after the close on 2026-09-30: consensus is roughly $50-51B revenue and $31-31.50 EPS (estimate, not yet reported). GS expects about 3% revenue upside to the Street.
Micron November-quarter (fiscal Q1) estimates: median sellside revenue $51.49B, gross margin 86.2%, EPS $31.83 (consensus estimates, not reported). GS expects a guide of $57.7B vs $56.7B consensus.
Prior May-quarter print (reported 6/24): revenue $41.5B reported vs $35.7B expected, gross margin 84.9% vs 81.9% expected. August-quarter guide was $49-51B.
Micron has beaten EPS by 10-30% over the last ~6 quarters. Investors expect SCA mix to somewhat limit the beat size this time.
Micron net cash is ~$24.4B and adjusted FCF last quarter was $18.3B.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The author's aside links DRAM price inflation to core PCE (+0.5% for 2026) and says a 10Y at 5.30% implies a corporate bond sale to fund the buildout may come soon. This is commentary by the ZeroHedge writer, not a Goldman view.

risk_factors: SCA mix limits spot-price upside and the size of the earnings beat.
The Street already expects a beat, so the stock needs more than 'in line' to repeat June's reaction.
Liquidity void in Korean memory names when Samsung and SK Hynix buybacks end in early October.
Data center construction delays: 60% of US data centers planned for 2027 completion have not started, mostly due to power constraints.
Deceleration in y/y and q/q growth in the November guide.
vol_and_positioning: Positioning into Micron's print is 'relatively balanced' per GS's Peter Callahan. MU is about 10% below its all-time high, while Samsung and Hynix are 20-40% below theirs.
Memory stocks in Asia have suffered from relative overweight positioning during intense de-grossing, per GS's Narain.

Samsung and SK Hynix buybacks are 87% and ~75% complete and both finish early October. Foreigners and retail were joint net sellers in September, raising liquidity void concerns once the buybacks end.
geopolitical: China's CXMT is cited as a supply threat to the memory industry.
CHIPS Act restrictions on buybacks are due to lift around the December 9 anniversary.
China industry supply/demand is one of Callahan's five talking points.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman expects a beat and a November guide above consensus ($57.7BN vs $56.7BN), with persistent DRAM/NAND tightness supporting pricing and mix.
tension_points.bear_case: A larger share of output under SCAs limits spot-price upside, so the beat may be smaller than the 10-30% EPS beats of the last ~6 quarters. With MU only ~10% off highs and a beat expected, the stock needs more than 'in line'.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A November-quarter guide at or below the Street, or a smaller-than-expected SCA coverage disclosure in the 10-K.

theme_stances.key_argument: Persistent memory supply-demand tightness drives another strong quarter, upside to consensus and robust guidance, though SCAs may cap the beat.
